status: G4 pilot: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-camel, in Chapters VI and IX (the desktop app only)
use: A dromedary of the caravans standing beside the camel gear in the quartermaster's court beyond the board (Chapters VI and IX).

generator.prompt: A dromedary camel of the Syrian desert caravans, mid-3rd century AD, standing square: all four long legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, neck curving up with the head level and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A tall single-humped camel about 1.9 metres at the top of the hump with a sandy-tan coat, darker shaggy hair on the hump, neck and upper legs, a woven red and ochre wool blanket over the hump held by a plain girth, and a plain rope halter. No saddle frame, no packs, no rider, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A sandy dromedary under a red and ochre blanket with tassels, held by a girth, in a rope halter, as asked; it came facing its +z and was processed a quarter turn round to face +x: 2.8 m long and 2.2 m high. In Chapters VI and IX it stands beside the camel gear, its blanket and long neck the plainest things in the court.
